target.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
target.body:
## Summary

Grounds assistant transcript text before session-context replay: an absolute path under the managed media dir that does not resolve to a real file is redacted to `[unverified media reference removed]`, keeping the surrounding prose. User text is never rewritten, and paths outside the managed media dir (code paths, host paths) are exempt so ordinary technical conversation is untouched.

Motivation is a live incident on a production gateway (2026-07-06): a bare 3-character inbound message ("Hey", no attachment, WhatsApp plugin disabled) produced an assistant turn containing `IMAGE:<media-dir>/whats-app-image-2026-07-06-...jpg` plus a detailed description of an image that never existed on disk or in the gateway inbound log. The session-context replay then compiled that fabricated text into every subsequent prompt (`context.compiled` / `prompt.submitted` in the trajectory), making the hallucination self-reinforcing for the rest of the session.

The invariant this leans on: legitimate inbound media never reaches prompts as a raw absolute path -- `media-note.ts` normalizes managed refs to `media://inbound/...`. So a raw absolute managed-media path inside *assistant* text is either fabricated or expired; both are unusable and safe to redact. This deliberately does not attempt free-text hallucination detection -- it only removes verifiably ungrounded media references, deterministically, with zero model calls.

Implementation: `redactUngroundedMediaRefs` in `src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.ts`, wired into `parseRecentConversationText` (assistant branch only) in `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, which serves `readRecentUserAssistantTextForSession` and its plugin-sdk consumers (e.g. the Telegram session transcript context). Handles the macOS `/private/var` twin, path-token boundaries (no substring matches inside longer paths or words), and trailing sentence punctuation; returns the same reference on no-op.

## Verification

- New colocated tests: 8 unit cases (fabricated ref redacted with prose kept, verified ref preserved, non-media absolute paths untouched, `/private` twin, token boundaries, trailing punctuation, mixed refs, no-op identity) plus a reader-level regression that replays the observed incident shape through `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` against real files in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (fabricated ref redacted; real-file ref and user text preserved verbatim).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`: 61 passed / 0 failed on this branch (includes the pre-existing 51 transcript reader tests, unchanged).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on touched files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: A hallucinated managed-media path in an assistant turn (fabricated `IMAGE:<media-dir>/...jpg` reference to a file that never existed) was replayed verbatim into subsequent prompt context, reinforcing the fabrication across the session.
Real environment tested: macOS 26 source checkout; reader-level regression executes the real transcript reader against a real on-disk session transcript and real files under a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media dir (no mocks in the replay path); incident evidence from a production macOS gateway trajectory (session ab2e822c, 2026-07-06 09:21 EDT).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: assistant entry text returned by `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` is `IMAGE:[unverified media reference removed] That's a serious setup. Original at <real file>.` -- the fabricated path is gone, the verified real-file ref and all prose survive, and the user entry containing the same fake path is returned unmodified.
Observed result after fix: 61 passed / 0 failed.
What was not tested: a live gateway restart/deploy with the incident session replayed end-to-end over Telegram; the fix is currently soaking on a fork deployment branch before fleet rollout.
